BiblicalUsage: zâmar means to trim (a vine). In Leviticus 25:3 we read, "Six years thou shalt sow thy field, and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard, and gather in the fruit thereof;". It appears again in Leviticus 25:4: "But in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land, a sabbath for the LORD..."
TheologicalSignificance: zamar is to trim (a vine), and I believe it shows me something true about the way God made the world.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
